Among voters self-reported as black, 62.7% are correctly classified, which rounds to 0.63.

I merged the voters with the census surname list and the voting-district data, then dropped any voter with a missing value. That left 8,021 of the 10,000 voters. For each voter I combined P(race | surname) from the surname list with P(race | residence) from the district data. I divided by each race's statewide share, which I computed from the district data weighted by population, and then normalised. I took the race with the highest resulting probability as the prediction. The prediction matched self-reported race for 62.7% of the black voters.

ANSWER: 0.63
